_comment: BERC Order 2026/22, published by notification memo 28.01.0000.012.04.003.26.2521 of 3 June
2026. The whole LT-A ladder rose. One day later, Reconsideration Order 2026/01 set aside the
increases to the lifeline and first step only, so slabs 1 and 2 below have a CLOSED knowledge
interval (3-4 June) while slabs 3-7 and the demand charge remain the answer today.
That asymmetry is the point of versioning components rather than schedules: an amended
instrument still governs every row it was not amended in. Resolving June 2026 with no asOf
returns 4.63 from the reconsideration order for the lifeline AND 8.50 from this order for the
second step, in one schedule assembled from two instruments.
Clause 2 of the notification states that existing demand charges are unchanged, which is why
the 42.00 Tk/kW/month rate is re-encoded here at the same value rather than inherited.
Clause 3 names Appendix-kha of this order as fixing the 2026 terms, applicability and
miscellaneous charges, and declares it an inseparable part of the tariff. That appendix is
NOT held. It is the most likely home of the VAT treatment and the prompt-payment rebate, and
both stay UNKNOWN until it is.

instrument.titleEn: Notification on the re-fixing of retail electricity tariff (Retail Electricity Tariff, 2026)
instrument.legalBasis: BERC Act 2003, ss. 22(kha) and 34, after a public hearing

evidence.locator: Retail Electricity Tariff 2026, section ka (LT), page 1; footnotes 2 and 3 and clauses 2-6, page 4

instrument.note: Effective from bill month June 2026. Signed by Md. Nazrul Islam Sarkar, Secretary, BERC.

knowledge.basis: BERC notification memo 28.01.0000.012.04.003.26.2521 published 3 June 2026; ceased to be the answer when memo 2569 published the reconsideration on 4 June

components.label: VAT
components.reason: Authoritative calculation rule not yet verified. This gazette states VAT only on the Table-2 miscellaneous service fees, condition (gha). Neither it nor the June 2026 instruments state VAT on the energy or demand charge — that rule belongs to VAT law rather than the tariff order, so the evidence chain runs through a second regulator. The universally quoted '5% on energy plus demand' is unsourced here.
components.wouldBeSettledBy: An NBR instrument, or an authentic postpaid bill showing the VAT base and its position in the order of operations

knowledge.basis: Absence established from the notification held; BERC Order 2026/22 Appendix-kha, which the notification names as fixing the miscellaneous charges, is not held

components.label: Prompt-payment rebate
components.reason: The 5% pay-by-due-date rebate that secondary calculators list appears in no instrument held. It is either in an appendix not yet obtained, a utility practice outside the tariff order, or calculator folklore.
components.wouldBeSettledBy: The 2026 counterpart of Table-2 (BERC Order 2026/22, Appendix-kha), or an authentic bill
